title: Which friend ran the hundred metres quicker?
description: Two friends train for a hundred metre race, and their times over a week are in two rows. The board adds each row, divides by seven runs, compares the means, and checks each total by adding in pairs.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare averages by finding each total and sharing it over the number of runs, and for times a smaller time is quicker. Watch for students who say one friend must be quicker because the lists look different.

video_script.why: The child has compared fair shares of two groups and now compares the average times of two runners.
video_script.substitution: Each runner's total time is shared equally over the number of runs, and the smaller average time is the quicker runner.
video_script.anchor: Two rows of running times in seconds for a week of runs, one row for each friend
video_script.payoff_line: They ran equally quickly on average

final_answer.value: They ran equally quickly on average: both means are 122 ÷ 7 ≈ 17.43 seconds
final_answer.spoken: they ran equally quickly on average, and both means are about seventeen point four three seconds

maths_rules: mean = total / number of runs = 122 / 7 = 17.43 seconds to two places for both
a smaller time is a quicker run; equal means so neither is quicker on average
video_script.design: Two rows of times. Each row is added to 122, shared over seven runs, and the two means are compared. The check adds each row again in pairs.
